tagline: Down the longest Main Street in the world to the Gulf.
intro: Highway 1 follows Bayou Lafourche south from Raceland, past shrimpers and tugboats, shipbuilding yards and small seafood restaurants, toward Port Fourchon at the southern tip of the state and the beach at Grand Isle. The bayou was an outlet of the Mississippi until a dam cut it off in 1904, and with a highway down each bank it is called the longest Main Street in the world.

The trail takes in other roads too, Highway 24 between Thibodaux and Houma and Highways 56 and 57 south from Houma past marshes and lakes to the Gulf. French, Spanish, English and German trappers and fishermen settled the bayou before the Acadians came and gave it its Cajun flavor.

moments.title: Lockport
moments.text: A canal meant to link Bayou Terrebonne with New Orleans got its locks here in 1850 and did a brisk trade until 1868, and what remains is a brick bulwark under the weeds.

moments.title: Leeville
moments.text: Founded in 1893 by survivors of the Chenier Caminada hurricane, the town had 297 producing oil wells in 1938, and around 70 percent of the wetlands about it have gone since 1932.

moments.title: Grand Isle
moments.text: Highway 1 begins on the main street of this barrier island town and runs 436 miles to the state's northwest corner, and its causeway is the only way onto the island by land.
